name: Autism Spectrum Disorder-Epilepsy-Arthrogryposis Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autism Spectrum Disorder-Epilepsy-Arthrogryposis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts consistent with autism spectrum disorder
Recurrent unprovoked seizures confirmed by clinical history and EEG abnormalities
Congenital joint contractures affecting two or more body areas
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Neuroimaging showing structural brain abnormalities such as cortical dysplasia or hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, and arthrogryposis) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by EEG and neuroimaging findings.

laboratory: Possible metabolic screening abnormalities in select cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing cortical dysplasia, hypoplasia, or delayed myelination
X-rays demonstrating joint contractures and bone deformities
genetic: Likely autosomal recessive or de novo mutations; specific gene not yet identified
other: Neurodevelopmental assessments confirming autism spectrum disorder

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy
Characteristic regression after normal early development

redFlags: Onset of seizures within first year of life
Presence of multiple congenital joint contractures at birth
Severe social communication deficits with repetitive behaviors
references: Orphanet: Autism spectrum disorder-epilepsy-arthrogryposis syndrome, ORPHA:370943
Clinical and Molecular Characterization of Autism Spectrum Disorder with Epilepsy and Arthrogryposis, Journal of Rare Disorders, 2024
Diagnostic Criteria for Autism Spectrum Disorder, DSM-5, American Psychiatric Association, 2013
